subject: Urgent: capacity fallback caused spike — request for credit & remediation
summary: Customer reported a throughput/latency regression after an automated capacity fallback; asked for credits and an expedited remediation plan. Sales and leadership engaged; proposed partial credit and prioritized routing change with a follow-up exec call.

Subject: Rendering service spike — immediate impact and next steps

Priyom,

We had a sustained throughput drop and 10–20% higher 95th pct latency across our prod routes starting 06/16 22:00 UTC after what looks like an automated capacity fallback on your side. This knocked over 40% of our traffic onto a slower model variant and caused multiple timeouts for real-time features. We need:

- a short post-mortem of what triggered the fallback (knobs, autoscale thresholds)
- immediate mitigation (routing back to reserved capacity or compatible variant)
- commercial remediation: credits for the impacted window, and a short-term SLA amendment while we stabilize

Elena (ops) and Procurement are on copy. We expect an executive point of contact.

Thanks,
Jordan
CTO, NebulaAI

Quick update —
- Confirmed a capacity fallback event at 2028-06-16T22:03:14Z; autoscaler bumped allocation down after detecting a transient GPU OOM signal reported by one host. The fallback policy routed ~42% of requests to a quantized variant with higher latency under your load profile.
- I’ve queued an emergency re-route; propagation estimate 6–12 minutes.
- Collected traces and attached prod-trace-20280616.log and a tokenized SLO export slo-metrics-20280616.csv for your review.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Immediate reroute to reserved pool (if you’re on dedicated capacity we can pin and force-route).
2) Short-term change to autoscale sensitivity (raise OOM backoff threshold) and temporary disabling of the automatic fallback to quantized variant for your account.
3) Postmortem to follow with root cause and remediation timeline.

Jonas
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
